subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & initial pricing — follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & initial pricing — follow-up

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the follow-ups we discussed so we can align on sizing and a ballpark price. Please confirm anything that’s off or missing.

Summary of Acme Health needs (as we understood them):
- Primary workload: clinical summarization and question answering over patient notes (mixed short prompts + multi-k token context).
- Expected monthly token volume: 1M-3M tokens/month (with growth to ~6M over 12 months).
- Peak/steady characteristics: steady baseline of ~5 concurrent sessions, spikes to ~50 concurrent during morning sync windows.
- Latency SLO: interactive sub-200ms for short prompts; <500ms acceptable for longer completions (up to 1k tokens).
- Model: open LLM (Redwood-verified 70B variant) — plan to use quantized FP16/INT8 runtime.

Questions we still need from you to finalize sizing/pricing:
1) Can you confirm 1M-3M tokens/month is the correct current range and whether that includes embeddings?
2) Typical completion size (tokens per request) and % of requests that hit long context (>=1k tokens)?
3) Any hard constraints on single-request P95 latency for the short prompts?
4) Procurement timeline and target budget range (monthly or $/1M tokens target).

Preliminary sizing guidance (tentative):
- Conservative reserved option (recommended for predictability): 2 x H100-equivalent GPUs (redundant pool) — handles ~120-200k tokens/sec aggregate depending on batching and model. Good for steady 5-50 concurrent users with low tail latency.
- Cost-balanced option: 4 x A100-similar GPUs — slightly lower peak single-request tail performance vs H100, but can be more cost-efficient depending on utilization and batching.
- High-throughput option: 8 x H100 — for sustained high concurrency and low latency at scale.

Initial unit-economics target discussion: you mentioned aiming for ~$900- $1,200 per 1M tokens as a target range for total cost of inference (including reserved capacity amortization, storage, network). We can often get below that for predictable, cacheable workloads with batching/caching optimizations; for long-context sensitive workloads the unit cost tends to be higher.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the token volume and long-context % so we can send a simple 2-option pricing (conservative vs cost-optimized) by EOD May 3.
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Marissa (SE) to go over workload profile and exact throughput tests (can you do May 4 or 5?).
- If procurement needs a formal TCO/quote, we’ll draft a one-page TCO and a draft MOU for Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: please attach any throughput logs or sample payloads (we can use acme_prod_latency_profile.csv if available).

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & initial pricing — follow-up

Thanks Marcus — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: current pilot uses ~1.2M tokens/month (this is LLM generation tokens only — embeddings tracked separately). We expect to expand to ~3M over Q3 and ~6M by end of year if performance and cost look good.
- Long-context: ~10% of requests hit >1k tokens today (summaries over full visit notes). Average completion is ~350 tokens.
- Latency: for short prompts we’d like P95 < 200ms; for long completions < 800ms is acceptable.
- Budget: procurement asked for a target of ~$1,000 / 1M tokens as a baseline estimate so they can compare to other vendors. They’re flexible on committed monthly cost if unit economics are favorable.
- Timeline: procurement is planning vendor selection by end of May, so we’d like a formal quote and MOU in the next two weeks.

I’m attaching the throughput logs and a short requirements spreadsheet (acme_requirements.xlsx) — gives example QPS by hour and a sample payload.

I can do a technical deep-dive with Marissa on May 4 at 10am PT.

—Emma

Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & initial pricing — follow-up

Thanks Emma — appreciate the logs and the budget target. Quick initial sizing + ballpark pricing options based on the profile you shared. These are rough and assume standard Redwood Dedicated configuration, quantized 70B model, and conservative batching. Final numbers will come after we validate with a short throughput test in the deep-dive.

Option A — Conservative / Predictable (recommended for procurement)- Reserved capacity: 2 x H100-class GPUs (redundant)- Target throughput: supports ~40-50 concurrent active sessions, typical peak QPS 150-250 with batching- Expected monthly amortized cost (infrastructure + support + license): ~$58,000/month- Implied unit cost: ~1,150 $/1M tokens at 1.2M/month; improves to ~600-900 $/1M tokens at 3-6M/month due to higher utilization + caching

Option B — Cost-optimized (higher GPU count, more utilization required)- Reserved capacity: 4 x A100-class GPUs- Target throughput: similar aggregate tokens/sec when heavily batched; slightly higher cost efficiency at steady high utilization- Expected monthly amortized cost: ~$46,000/month- Implied unit cost: ~900 $/1M tokens at 1.2M/month; ~450-700 $/1M tokens at 3-6M/month (depends on batching/caching)

Option C — Low-latency / high-throughput- Reserved capacity: 8 x H100-class GPUs- Target throughput: very low tail latency under heavy concurrency, supports large spikes with <200ms P95 for short prompts- Expected monthly amortized cost: ~$180,000+/month- Implied unit cost: >1,000 $/1M tokens at low utilization but drops with heavy sustained utilization

Key notes / levers to improve unit economics:
- Batching: effective for short prompts; careful batching policy can cut token cost significantly without harming UX.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated patient prompts (e.g., same note viewed repeatedly) we can reduce repeated compute.
- Quantization profile: INT8 paths reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; we’ll validate model quality in the deep-dive.

Next steps from our side:
1) Align on Option A vs B vs C (we can also propose hybrid: baseline reserve A with burst to shared pools).
2) Technical deep-dive May 4 @ 10am PT — we’ll run a short throughput experiment to validate the numbers above.
3) After the experiment we’ll deliver a 1-page TCO and a draft MOU for Dedicated capacity (includes SLA, support, and on/off-ramps).

I’ll bring Logan (infra) to the call to cover autoscaling and burst policies. Marcus, I’ll loop in a quick test plan by EOD May 3.

—Marissa
